title: Session cookies vs JWT for a new internal service
notes: Clean decision session weighing two auth strategies and landing on one with explicit reasoning.

turns.text: For the new billing-service, should we do session cookies or JWTs for auth? It only talks to our own frontend, nothing cross-domain.

Since it's same-origin and only serves our own frontend, session cookies are the simpler and safer choice — httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies avoid the need to think about token storage in localStorage/sessionStorage, which is vulnerable to XSS exfiltration.
What about revocation? I've heard JWTs are hard to revoke.

That's actually another point in favor of sessions here — with server-side session storage, revocation is just deleting the session row, immediate and simple. Stateless JWTs would need a blocklist or short expiry plus refresh complexity to get the same effect.
Any downside to sessions we should note for later?

The main one is horizontal scaling — session storage needs to be shared (e.g. Redis) across instances, whereas JWTs are self-contained. Not a concern at our current single-region, low-instance-count scale, but worth revisiting if billing-service ever needs to scale out significantly.
Fine, let's go with cookies then.
Going with httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict session cookies backed by server-side session storage for billing-service.

gold_atoms.text: Use httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict session cookies (not JWTs) for billing-service auth, since it's same-origin and only serves the team's own frontend.
Session cookies avoid the need to store tokens in localStorage/sessionStorage, which is vulnerable to XSS exfiltration.
With server-side session storage, revoking access is as simple as deleting the session row; stateless JWTs would need a blocklist or short expiry plus refresh complexity to achieve the same effect.

Session storage needs to be shared (e.g. Redis) across instances to scale horizontally, unlike self-contained JWTs — not a concern at the current single-region, low-instance-count scale, but worth revisiting if billing-service scales out significantly.
